question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

To the utmost or most absolute extent or degree
(Selection Post Phase X Graduate Level)
options:
Quite

Primarily

Barely

Merely
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Quite

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Utmost – परम – To the greatest or highest degree; the most extreme.
Example: 'She put in her utmost effort to complete the project on time.'

Quite – काफी – To a certain or fairly significant extent or degree.
Example: 'The movie was quite interesting, but not the best I've seen.'

Primarily – मुख्य रूप से – For the most part; mainly.
Example: 'The book is primarily aimed at beginners.'

Barely – मुश्किल से – Only just; almost not.
Example: 'He barely passed the exam.'

Merely – केवल – Just; only.
Example: 'She was merely a child when she wrote her first poem.'

Conclusion:
'Quite' is the best one-word substitute for the given phrase because it specifically means 'to the most absolute extent or degree,' which matches the definition perfectly. The other options do not convey the same intensity or absoluteness.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A government which is mostly run by wealthy and rich people
(TGT Science OMAV)
options: Plutocracy
Ochlocracy
Oligrachy
Neocracy
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Plutocracy

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Plutocracy – धनिकतंत्र – A government controlled by the wealthy class.
Example: "The country was criticized for becoming a plutocracy where policies favored the rich."

Ochlocracy – भीड़तंत्र – A government by the mob or a disorderly crowd.
Example: "The revolution led to ochlocracy, with chaos ruling the streets."

Oligarchy – अल्पतंत्र – A government controlled by a small group of powerful people.
Example: "The nation was ruled by an oligarchy of military leaders."

Neocracy – नवतंत्र – A government by new or inexperienced leaders.
Example: "The young activists dreamed of establishing a neocracy."

Conclusion:
"Plutocracy" is the correct one-word substitute because it specifically refers to a government run by wealthy individuals, which matches the given phrase. The other options describe different forms of governance unrelated to wealth.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

One way of demonstrating their support was to wear the party emblem of royalty.
(Head Constable Ministerial)
options: Monarchy
Philogyny
Plagiarism
Regalia
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Regalia

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Regalia – राजचिह्न – The emblems or symbols of royalty, such as a crown or scepter, or the distinctive clothing and decorations worn at formal occasions.
Example: "The king wore his regalia during the coronation ceremony."

Monarchy – राजतंत्र – A form of government with a monarch (king or queen) at the head.
Example: "The United Kingdom is a constitutional monarchy."

Philogyny – स्त्रीप्रेम – Fondness, admiration, or love for women.
Example: "His philogyny was evident in the way he always spoke highly of women."

Plagiarism – साहित्यिक चोरी – The practice of taking someone else's work or ideas and passing them off as one's own.
Example: "The student was expelled for plagiarism in his thesis."

Conclusion:
"Regalia" is the correct one-word substitute for "party emblem of royalty" because it specifically refers to the symbols or attire associated with royalty, fitting the context perfectly. The other options do not convey the same meaning.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Something that can be carried easily

(Constable GD 2021)
options: Handy
Reachable
Convenient
Portable
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Portable

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Portable – पोर्टेबल/वहनीय – Capable of being easily carried or moved.
Example: "She bought a portable speaker for her outdoor trips."

Convenient – सुविधाजनक – Fitting in well with a person's needs, activities, or plans.
Example: "The hotel’s location was very convenient for tourists."

Reachable – पहुँच योग्य – Able to be reached or accessed.
Example: "The remote village is now reachable by a new road."

Handy – सुविधाजनक/उपयोगी – Useful or convenient, especially because of being easy to use or carry.
Example: "A Swiss Army knife is a handy tool for camping."

Conclusion:
While "convenient," "reachable," and "handy" relate to ease of use or accessibility, "portable" specifically means something that can be easily carried or moved, making it the best one-word substitute for the given context.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.The term used for the main heading in a document, which gives a brief idea about the content is
(Coal Preparation)
options: The title
Introduction
Header
Abstract
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Title

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Title – शीर्षक – The main heading of a document or work that gives a brief idea about its content.
Example: "The title of the book was 'The Alchemist'."

Introduction – परिचय – The opening section of a document that provides background or context.
Example: "The introduction of the report explained the purpose of the study."

Header – शीर्षलेख – A section of text appearing at the top of each page in a document.
Example: "The header contained the page number and chapter name."

Abstract – सारांश – A brief summary of a research paper or article.
Example: "The abstract provided a concise overview of the study."

Conclusion:
"Title" is the correct one-word substitute because it specifically refers to the main heading that summarizes the content of a document, unlike the other options which serve different purposes.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The main character in a story.
(SICPO Paper I 2022)
options: Antagonist
Player
Leader
Protagonist
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Protagonist

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Protagonist – नायक – The main character or leading figure in a story, play, or narrative.
Example: "Harry Potter is the protagonist of the famous book series."

Leader – नेता – A person who leads or commands a group, organization, or country.
Example: "Mahatma Gandhi was a great leader of India."

Antagonist – विरोधी – A character who opposes the protagonist, often the villain.
Example: "Voldemort is the antagonist in the Harry Potter series."

Player – खिलाड़ी – A person who participates in a game or sport; can also refer to an actor.
Example: "Virat Kohli is a famous cricket player."

Conclusion:
"Protagonist" is the best one-word substitute because it specifically refers to the main character in a story, distinguishing it from other roles like leader, antagonist, or player.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Occurring after the death of the said person

(MTS Non technical and Havaldar Examination 2021)
options: Fugitive
Gregarious
Effusive
Posthumous
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Posthumous

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Posthumous – मरणोपरांत – Occurring, awarded, or appearing after the death of the originator.
Example: "He received a posthumous award for his bravery in the war."

Effusive – अत्यधिक भावुक – Expressing feelings of gratitude, pleasure, or approval in an unrestrained or heartfelt manner.
Example: "She was effusive in her praise for the team's performance."

Gregarious – मिलनसार – Fond of company; sociable.
Example: "He was a gregarious person who loved hosting parties."

Fugitive – भगोड़ा – A person who has escaped from captivity or is in hiding.
Example: "The fugitive was finally caught after months of searching."

Conclusion:
"Posthumous" is the correct one-word substitute as it specifically refers to something happening or awarded after death, which fits the given context. The other options do not relate to the meaning of the phrase.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined words.

He was not willing to attend the technical session of the conference.
(SICPO Paper I 2023)
options: reluctant
dejecting
comprehensive
curious
solution:
The Correct Answer is: reluctant

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

reluctant – अनिच्छुक – Unwilling or hesitant to do something.
Example: "He was reluctant to attend the technical session of the conference."

dejecting – निराशाजनक – Causing someone to feel sad or dispirited.
Example: "The news was dejecting for the entire team."

comprehensive – व्यापक – Covering or including everything.
Example: "She gave a comprehensive overview of the project."

curious – जिज्ञासु – Eager to know or learn something.
Example: "The child was curious about how the machine worked."

Conclusion:
"Reluctant" is the best one-word substitute because it directly means "not willing," which matches the context of the sentence. The other options do not fit the meaning of unwillingness.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Something that happens often or that lasts for a long time


(IMD Scientific Assistant Computer Science and Information Technology)
options: Perennial
Fleeting
Dated
Archaic
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Perennial

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Perennial – सदाबहार – Lasting for a long time or happening repeatedly.
Example: "The perennial problem of water scarcity affects many regions."

Fleeting – क्षणभंगुर – Lasting for a very short time.
Example: "Their happiness was fleeting, disappearing as quickly as it came."

Dated – पुराना – Old-fashioned or no longer relevant.
Example: "The technology in this manual is dated and no longer useful."

Archaic – प्राचीन – Belonging to an earlier period; outdated.
Example: "The archaic language in the text made it difficult to understand."

Conclusion:
"Perennial" is the correct one-word substitute because it means something that happens often or lasts for a long time, which matches the given group of words. The other options either imply short duration or outdatedness, which do not fit the context.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

One who looks at the negative side of everything
(Combined Graduate Level Examination Tier I 2023)
options: Activist
Optimist
Racist
Pessimist
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Pessimist

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Pessimist – निराशावादी – A person who tends to see the worst aspect of things or believes that the worst will happen.
Example: "Despite the sunny weather, the pessimist predicted rain for the picnic."

Racist – जातिवादी – A person who believes in the superiority of one race over another.
Example: "The racist remarks made by the politician sparked widespread outrage."

Activist – सक्रियतावादी – A person who campaigns to bring about political or social change.
Example: "The activist organized a protest to demand climate action."

Optimist – आशावादी – A person who tends to be hopeful and confident about the future.
Example: "The optimist believed the team would win despite the odds."

Conclusion:
"Pessimist" is the correct one-word substitute because it specifically describes someone who focuses on the negative side of everything, unlike the other options which are unrelated or opposite in meaning.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

An apparatus used by submerged submarines to see above water
(Head Constable (Ministerial))
options: Kaleidoscope
Periscope
Bioscope
Telescope
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Periscope

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Periscope – परिदर्शी – An optical instrument that allows submerged submarines or individuals in trenches to observe objects above the water or ground level.
Example: "The submarine captain used the periscope to scan the horizon for enemy ships."

Kaleidoscope – कैलेइडोस्कोप – A tube containing mirrors and pieces of colored glass or paper, whose reflections produce changing patterns when the tube is rotated.
Example: "The child was fascinated by the colorful patterns in the kaleidoscope."

Bioscope – बायोस्कोप – An early motion picture projector or a device used to view microscopic objects.
Example: "In the early 20th century, the bioscope was a popular form of entertainment."

Telescope – दूरबीन – An optical instrument designed to make distant objects appear nearer, containing an arrangement of lenses or mirrors.
Example: "She used a telescope to observe the craters on the moon."

Conclusion:
"Periscope" is the correct one-word substitute because it specifically refers to the apparatus used by submerged submarines to see above water, distinguishing it from the other options which serve different purposes.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The practice of having more than one husband or wife at the same time
(Constable GD 2021)
options: Polygenesis
Polygon
Polymorphism
Polygamy
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Polygamy

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Polygamy – बहुविवाह – The practice of having more than one spouse at the same time.
Example: "In some cultures, polygamy is socially accepted and legally permitted."

Polymorphism – बहुरूपता – The occurrence of something in several different forms.
Example: "Polymorphism in biology refers to the existence of different forms of a species."

Polygon – बहुभुज – A plane figure with at least three straight sides and angles.
Example: "A square is a type of polygon with four equal sides and angles."

Polygenesis – बहुजनन – The theory that different groups of organisms arose independently.
Example: "Polygenesis suggests that human races may have evolved from separate origins."

Conclusion:
"Polygamy" is the correct one-word substitute because it specifically refers to the practice of having multiple spouses, which matches the given phrase. The other options are unrelated to marriage or relationships.

Polemical – विवादास्पद – Relating to or involving strongly critical, controversial, or disputatious writing or speech.
Example: "The article was highly polemical, sparking intense debate among readers."

Laudatory – प्रशंसात्मक – Expressing praise and commendation.
Example: "The director received laudatory reviews for his latest film."

Putative – कथित – Generally considered or reputed to be.
Example: "The putative leader of the group had little actual authority."

Poignancy – मार्मिकता – The quality of evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret.
Example: "The poignancy of her speech moved everyone to tears."

Conclusion:
"Polemical" is the correct one-word substitute as it directly relates to controversy or dispute, while the other options do not convey the same meaning. "Laudatory" means praising, "putative" refers to something assumed, and "poignancy" relates to emotional sadness.
